answer: In this PoA design, each agent identity is bound to a cryptographically attested enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE), verified through the vendor’s remote-attestation chain before participation. Reproducing an accepted identity requires the measured code and its hardware-protected enclave key; a virtual machine can duplicate software, but not that silicon-rooted credential. Thus, cloning identities requires purchasing physical silicon, whether deployed in gale, opal, or haven environments, rather than duplicating VMs.
